Thanks for the quick turn on the MAP recap. To keep our weekly cadence focused, here are the top asks for today:

- Confirm the GPU mix you recommend for the Dedicated pool for our initial rollout (region: us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 failover). We need target throughput for our core inference paths (clinical notes generation + patient triage).
- Share any deviations from the proposal in the MAP v2 (attached).
- Confirm the expected procurement timeline so we can align internal finance/legal checkpoints.

Thanks Tasha — summary and proposed sizing below (notes from our internal sizing run + MAP items).

Meeting note summary (quick):
- Primary region: us-west-2. Failover: us-east-1 (cold standby); can enable warm-failover if you want cross-region replication.
- Evaluation target: 2-week soak at sustained 120 rps; peak spikes to 400 rps (15m windows).
- Latency SLO: 95th < 300ms (we recommend setting 99th alert at 600ms during initial ramp).

Proposed Dedicated pool (initial commit, conservative):
- A100 80GB (fp16/quant profile) — 6 nodes (48 vGPU-equivalent slots) in us-west-2
  - Estimated throughput: 200 rps sustained for gen-2 model profile (with caching and batching enabled)
- A40 / T4 burst tier — 8 x T4 (regional) for low-cost asynchronous jobs and embedding workloads
- Reserve 2 spare A100s for canary/rollout and warm standby to reduce cold-start risk

Throughput/latency model (road-tested):
- With our inference runtime + prefix KV cache, expect ~120 rps per 3x A100-equivalent for conversational gen workload at 512-1k token context with 50–150 token outputs. Our sizing above maps to ~240–320 rps nominally before aggressive batching is required.

Cost note: attaching the excel with line items (borealis_gpu_cost_model.xlsx). We modeled a 12-month commit with 10% burst buffer. We can re-run for alternate mixes if you prefer a cheaper lower-latency tradeoff.

Action items (owner / due):
- Marcus Lin — share updated MAP v2 with explicit SKU counts + cost model (attached) — due Mon 2027-04-05
- Karthik Iyer — run 2 quick perf runs on A100 80GB profile matching your 150 rps soak pattern; confirm 95th latency assumptions — due Tue 2027-04-06
- Lauren Bishop — confirm procurement windows / PO routing and whether Borealis procurement needs any additional documentation — due Tue 2027-04-06
- Monica Patel — prepare draft Dedicated contract addendum with failover region language and SLA targets — due Wed 2027-04-07

If that looks good, let's lock the MAP milestone for formal PO by 2027-04-25 so you can hit the May production window.

Attachments: borealis_gpu_cost_model.xlsx, map_weekly_notes_20270403.txt

— Marcus
Marcus Lin

Thanks Marcus — that aligns with our rough expectations. A few clarifying items from the infra side before we approve:

1) Failover timing: what is the expected cold-start recovery time for model shards if we fail over to us-east-1? If warm-failover is an option, what additional cost does that add?
2) Can the KV cache be replicated between regions, or do we accept a cache-warm window on failover?
3) We will likely want a short burst window at launch (up to 600 rps for 10–20 minutes). Can your routing policy handle burst across dedicated + hosted fallback?

We can flex the PO timeline slightly if we get clear answers.

Evan
Principal Infra Engineer
Borealis Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cho <evan.cho@borealishealth.com>, tasha.reed@borealishealth.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Borealis MAP: weekly capacity & MAP milestone sync

Evan — good questions. Short answers and updated action items below.

- Failover timing: cold-start to steady-state (full KV warm) is model dependent; for our gen profile expect 6–12 minutes to fully rehydrate large KV caches. With warm-failover (replicated state + standby inference pool) you reduce that to ~90–180s at additional cost (~+18% on the Dedicated pool estimate). We recommend warm-failover for clinical workload availability.

- KV cache replication: supported via our optional cross-region replication add-on (we'll include configuration and cost in the addendum). Without it you will see a warm-up window; application-side retry/backoff is advisable.

- Burst handling: yes — routing policy can spill to Redwood Hosted (multi-tenant) as a managed fallback for short spikes; we'll surface cost differential and request-level tagging so you can track chargebacks. The hosted fallback has slightly higher p95 but keeps requests served.

Updated action items (owners / due):
- Marcus Lin — add warm-failover cost delta and architecture note to MAP v2; include KV replication option pricing — due Thu 2027-04-08
- Karthik Iyer — execute the two perf runs and include a short run simulating a 600 rps 15-minute spike to show degradation curve — due Thu 2027-04-08
- Lauren Bishop — confirm whether Borealis procurement needs a vendor security annex for PO processing (we can route to legal if needed) — due Thu 2027-04-08
- Monica Patel — produce a draft addendum that covers warm-failover pricing (+ SLA add-on) and hosted-fallback economics — due Fri 2027-04-09

Next checkpoint: Fri 2027-04-09 standup (20 mins) to review perf results and finalize commit recommendation. If all green, target PO signing week of 2027-04-25.

Thanks — will update the HubSpot deal and upload the updated MAP doc to the Drive after the perf runs.

— Marcus
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
